logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, validation errors show internal field keys instead of visible field names: examples include profile Website, release Tag name/Title, branch rename, protected-tag pattern and repository Default Branch. The input can be correctly rejected while the banner says form.Website, form.TagName or a similar untranslated key.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Validate constructs form.<GoField> labels; Website has no matching translated field label and URL validation appends its internal Url message argument.
reproductionPaths: Gitea’s invalid protected-tag pattern is correctly rejected, but the visible validation alert exposes the internal key `form.NamePattern` instead of the form's user-facing “Tag Pattern” label.
In Gitea, creating a repository with an invalid Default Branch name shows an error that names the field with the internal key form.DefaultBranch instead of the visible 'Default Branch' label.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, branch protection uses filename-like patterns to identify branches subject to a rule. Saving a malformed pattern returns an Internal Server Error but nevertheless persists the rule, leaving an invalid saved configuration despite the failed response.
logicalBugs.rootCause: ProtectBranchForm gives RuleName only Required validation, and SettingsProtectedBranchPost persists it without compiling the branch pattern first; later rendering/matching encounters the malformed rule.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, branch protection uses filename-like patterns to identify branches subject to a rule. Saving a malformed pattern returns an Internal Server Error but nevertheless persists the rule, leaving an invalid saved configuration despite the failed response.

logicalBugs.description: A Gitea repository’s Public Access settings describe Anonymous Read as allowing access without signing in. When the whole site requires sign-in, that option still saves with the same description even though logged-out access is blocked, giving no indication that the site-wide requirement overrides the repository setting.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The public-access template describes anonymous-read without accounting for the site RequireSignInView override that still gates access.
reproductionPaths: A Gitea repository’s Public Access settings describe Anonymous Read as allowing access without signing in. When the whole site requires sign-in, that option still saves with the same description even though logged-out access is blocked, giving no indication that the site-wide requirement overrides the repository setting.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a public repository with default unit permissions has no Public Access settings link. The page works at its known URL, and saving a non-default grant makes the missing navigation entry appear.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The navbar exposes the link only when the repository is private or HasAnyUnitPublicAccess, excluding public repositories before an explicit nondefault policy exists.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, a public repository with default unit permissions has no Public Access settings link. The page works at its known URL, and saving a non-default grant makes the missing navigation entry appear.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, generating a template with only metadata selected creates an empty default branch. The setup commands omit the branch, and the visible New File and Upload File links lead to 404 pages.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Generate repository setup initializes the default branch in the Git-content path rather than supplying one for metadata-only generation, so the empty repository links and quick guide interpolate an empty branch.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, generating a template with only metadata selected creates an empty default branch. The setup commands omit the branch, and the visible New File and Upload File links lead to 404 pages.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, add New Rule with an existing protected-branch pattern updates the original rule using the new form defaults without warning or confirmation beforehand. This removes its saved approval requirement and administrator enforcement.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The new-rule branch explicitly looks up the existing RuleName and updates it instead of rejecting a duplicate.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, add New Rule with an existing protected-branch pattern updates the original rule using the new form defaults without warning or confirmation beforehand. This removes its saved approval requirement and administrator enforcement.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, with branch push disabled but an unprotected-file pattern allowing a specific path, the web editor still disables/refuses direct commits to that branch. Editing an existing allowed file and creating/uploading an allowed new file are affected even though the protection policy allows that exception.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CanCommitToBranch uses only protectedBranch.CanUserPush and never evaluates GetUnprotectedFilePatterns for the file being edited/created, though the write service supports that exception.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, with branch push disabled and an existing file matched by the rule's unprotected-file pattern, the web editor disables direct commit and forces the new-branch option, despite the rule help promising that matching files can be changed directly by users with write access.

In Gitea, with branch push disabled, the web New File and Upload File flows refuse to commit directly to the branch even when the new path matches the rule's unprotected-file pattern, although the rule help says matching files can be changed directly by users with write access.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, with a branch rule whose protected file patterns include README.md, editing or deleting README.md directly is blocked, but renaming it in the web editor commits directly and removes README.md from the branch.
logicalBugs.rootCause: verify branch checks the destination treePath against protected patterns but does not protect the original fromTreePath being removed by a rename.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, with a branch rule whose protected file patterns include README.md, editing or deleting README.md directly is blocked, but renaming it in the web editor commits directly and removes README.md from the branch.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, branch-protection rules can prevent changes to matching file paths. Attempting to delete such a protected file through the web editor opens a full-page Internal Server Error instead of retaining the deletion form with an explanation that the rule forbids the operation.
logicalBugs.rootCause: DeleteFilePost sends protected path rejection through its generic DeleteRepoFile ServerError path instead of translating ErrFilePathProtected into an in-form message.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, branch-protection rules can prevent changes to matching file paths. Attempting to delete such a protected file through the web editor opens a full-page Internal Server Error instead of retaining the deletion form with an explanation that the rule forbids the operation.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when New Repository is submitted with Initialize Repository and Make repository a template ticked but another field is invalid, the re-rendered form has both boxes unticked, so correcting the error silently creates an empty, non-template repository.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CreatePost re-renders on HasError with setup defaults rather than reconstructing the submitted initialization and template checkboxes.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when New Repository is submitted with Initialize Repository and Make repository a template ticked but another field is invalid, the re-rendered form has both boxes unticked, so correcting the error silently creates an empty, non-template repository.

logicalBugs.description: A Gitea branch-protection rule controls requirements for accepting proposed code changes, including how many approvals are needed. If the user enters a negative approval count and saves, the form correctly rejects that count but returns with the other edited rule fields reset. The failure is losing those unrelated draft policy settings during validation, rather than accepting the invalid approval count.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Validation failures flash an error and redirect to the GET editor, which reloads a saved/default rule instead of preserving the entered fields.
reproductionPaths: When a branch protection rule is saved with a negative required-approvals value, Gitea shows the validation error but redirects to a form that has lost every other field the user entered.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea’s branch-protection form's help text recommends `/docs/**/*.txt` as a protected file pattern, but patterns are matched as typed against repository paths that never start with `/`, so that pattern protects nothing.
logicalBugs.rootCause: IsProtectedFile matches lpath directly against compiled expressions without adding/removing a root slash, despite documentation showing root-prefixed patterns.
reproductionPaths: Gitea’s branch-protection form's help text recommends `/docs/**/*.txt` as a protected file pattern, but patterns are matched as typed against repository paths that never start with `/`, so that pattern protects nothing.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s repository Settings → Collaborators, the Teams search prints each team's overall access mode as '<mode> access'. General Access teams store that mode as none and keep their real rights per unit, so a team with Code: Write is labelled 'none access'.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The picker interpolates item.permission; General Access teams do not carry a concrete per-unit role in that response, so the fallback none label misrepresents them.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s repository Settings → Collaborators, the Teams search prints each team's overall access mode as '<mode> access'. General Access teams store that mode as none and keep their real rights per unit, so a team with Code: Write is labelled 'none access'.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, in repository settings, click Update Avatar without selecting an image. The response exposes a raw Avatar.Open filesystem error instead of explaining that an image must first be chosen; the missing-file condition is presented as an internal failure.
logicalBugs.rootCause: UpdateAvatarSetting checks only whether form.Avatar is nil, then opens it without checking for an empty filename/size. A nonnil empty bound upload reaches Avatar.Open and its raw wrapped error is flashed.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, in repository settings, click Update Avatar without selecting an image. The response exposes a raw Avatar.Open filesystem error instead of explaining that an image must first be chosen; the missing-file condition is presented as an internal failure.

logicalBugs.description: On a Gitea repository's Branches page, a collaborator with Write (not Admin) access sees the 'Switch default branch' icon next to the default branch, but it links to repository settings, which return 404 Page Not Found for non-admins.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The branch list renders the switch-default link under branch write visibility rather than the repository administration permission required by its destination.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea repository's Branches page, a collaborator with Write (not Admin) access sees the 'Switch default branch' icon next to the default branch, but it links to repository settings, which return 404 Page Not Found for non-admins.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a protected branch’s push allowlist chooses which collaborators may push changes. The picker offers read-only collaborators even though they cannot be saved in that list: selecting one and saving reports success, but reopening the rule shows that the selection was dropped.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The settings editor fills Users from GetRepoReaders, while the persistence path filters push allowlist members by write capability. Thus Read choices appear selectable but are dropped.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, a protected branch’s push allowlist chooses which collaborators may push changes. The picker offers read-only collaborators even though they cannot be saved in that list: selecting one and saving reports success, but reopening the rule shows that the selection was dropped.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, if the recipient creates a repository with the same name while a transfer is pending, clicking Accept Transfer shows a full-page 500 Internal Server Error instead of explaining the name conflict. The API accept endpoint also returns 500.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Acceptance forwards transfer failures through generic server-error handling rather than translating ErrRepoAlreadyExist when a recipient creates the same name after initiation.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, if the recipient creates a repository with the same name while a transfer is pending, clicking Accept Transfer shows a full-page 500 Internal Server Error instead of explaining the name conflict. The API accept endpoint also returns 500.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when a user can read a repository's Projects but not its Issues, the project board still shows New Issue, Labels and Milestones buttons, and each opens a 404 page. The repository header correctly hides Issues for that user.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The board template emits issue labels/milestones/new-issue controls without requiring permission to the Issues unit, although the target routes enforce it.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when a user can read a repository's Projects but not its Issues, the project board still shows New Issue, Labels and Milestones buttons, and each opens a 404 page. The repository header correctly hides Issues for that user.

logicalBugs.description: A Gitea repository generated from a template with Git Content has the template's LICENSE file byte for byte, but its sidebar has no license link and the license API returns none, while the template, forks and normally created repositories show it.
logicalBugs.rootCause: GenerateGitContent writes the copied tree but does not schedule the license updater used by ordinary pushes/creation; a later ordinary commit triggers detection.
reproductionPaths: A Gitea repository generated from a template with Git Content has the template's LICENSE file byte for byte, but its sidebar has no license link and the license API returns none, while the template, forks and normally created repositories show it.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s repository Settings > Basic Settings, submitting an invalid repository name shows the right validation error but redraws the form from the saved values, so the other edits made in the same submission (description, website, template checkbox) are lost.
logicalBugs.rootCause: handleSettingsPostUpdate renders tplSettingsOptions on name failure; template inputs still read Repository, so RenderWithErr form values do not retain other edits.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s repository Settings > Basic Settings, submitting an invalid repository name shows the right validation error but redraws the form from the saved values, so the other edits made in the same submission (description, website, template checkbox) are lost.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, in Settings > Tags, an empty Tag Pattern is rejected, but a pattern of only spaces or tabs is accepted with a success message and saved as an empty pattern that protects no tag. Editing an existing working rule to whitespace likewise reports success and silently removes its protection.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Required/GlobOrRegexPattern validation runs on the untrimmed NamePattern, then New/EditProtectedTagPost trims it before saving without checking again for empty.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, in Settings > Tags, an empty Tag Pattern is rejected, but a pattern of only spaces or tabs is accepted with a success message and saved as an empty pattern that protects no tag. Editing an existing working rule to whitespace likewise reports success and silently removes its protection.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, with the organization setting 'Repository admin can add and remove access for teams' turned off, a non-owner who gets repository admin through an Administrator-access team still sees the team controls under Settings > Collaborators and can add or remove teams, including their own.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The AddTeam/DeleteTeam policy checks Repo.IsOwner/Permission.IsOwner, whose team-derived owner access can include administrator teams; it does not explicitly verify organization Owners membership.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, with the organization setting 'Repository admin can add and remove access for teams' turned off, a non-owner who gets repository admin through an Administrator-access team still sees the team controls under Settings > Collaborators and can add or remove teams, including their own.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, transferring a private repository to a user with no access to it quietly adds that user as a Read collaborator so they can review the transfer. When the recipient rejects the transfer, that access is never removed, so they can keep reading the private repository's code after the transfer is gone.
logicalBugs.rootCause: StartRepositoryTransfer adds the recipient as a Read collaborator, while RejectRepositoryTransfer resets status and deletes only the transfer record without deleting that collaboration.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, transferring a private repository to a user with no access to it quietly adds that user as a Read collaborator so they can review the transfer. When the recipient rejects the transfer, that access is never removed, so they can keep reading the private repository's code after the transfer is gone.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, protected-tag deletion follows the tag creator’s allowlist status instead of the person deleting it. A non-allowed Write collaborator can delete a tag created by an allowed user, while an allowed user can be refused deletion of a tag created outside the rule.
logicalBugs.rootCause: DeleteReleaseByID passes rel.PublisherID to IsUserAllowedToControlTag rather than doer.ID; unauthorized users can delete allowed publishers tags and allowed users cannot delete other publishers tags.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, with a protected-tag rule (for example release-*) that allows only certain users, a Write collaborator who isn't allowed is correctly blocked from creating a matching tag but can still delete an existing one from the Tags page or the API. The delete check uses the tag's original publisher instead of the person deleting it, so deleting a tag published by an allowed user always passes.

In Gitea, deleting a tag that matches a protected-tag rule checks whether the tag's creator is allowed by the rule, not the person deleting it. So a collaborator on the rule's allowlist is refused ("The tag name is protected.") when deleting a matching tag created by a user who isn't on it.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on Settings > Collaborators, if a role change is rejected by the server (for example an administrator who lowered their own role to Read then picks Administrator again without refreshing), the role menu still switches to the chosen role and no error appears. The menu updates whatever the server responds; permissions themselves are enforced correctly.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The dropdown awaits POST but never checks response.ok; fetch resolves on HTTP errors, so the chosen label and last-value are committed as though the request succeeded.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, on Settings > Collaborators, if a role change is rejected by the server (for example an administrator who lowered their own role to Read then picks Administrator again without refreshing), the role menu still switches to the chosen role and no error appears. The menu updates whatever the server responds; permissions themselves are enforced correctly.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when a draft release uses a tag name that a protected-tag rule doesn't allow the user to create, clicking Publish Release from the Edit Release page replaces the form with a full-page 500 Internal Server Error, and the unsaved title and notes are lost. Creating the same release from New Release shows a readable error instead.
logicalBugs.rootCause: EditReleasePost handles every UpdateRelease failure with ServerError, unlike NewReleasePost which classifies ErrProtectedTagName and re-renders feedback.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when a draft release uses a tag name that a protected-tag rule doesn't allow the user to create, clicking Publish Release from the Edit Release page replaces the form with a full-page 500 Internal Server Error, and the unsaved title and notes are lost. Creating the same release from New Release shows a readable error instead.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, in an archived repository, the wiki (repository documentation) hides its create and edit buttons, but opening the wiki's New Page (or Edit) URL directly still shows an editable form with Save Page. Saving replaces the page with a full 404 instead of saying the repository is archived and read-only.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Wiki GET rendering can dispatch to edit/new form before enforcing archival write state, while POST uses RepoMustNotBeArchived and responds 404.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, in an archived repository, the wiki hides its create and edit buttons, but opening the wiki's New Page (or Edit) URL directly still shows an editable form with Save Page. Saving replaces the page with a full 404 instead of saying the repository is archived and read-only.

logicalBugs.description: In a Gitea repository's branch protection settings, a rule's Protected Branch Name Pattern made only of spaces is accepted with a success message and saved as a blank-looking rule. An empty pattern is rejected, but spaces aren't trimmed.
logicalBugs.rootCause: SettingsProtectedBranchPost checks f.RuleName == empty without trimming and then persists f.RuleName verbatim.
reproductionPaths: In a Gitea repository's branch protection settings, a rule's Protected Branch Name Pattern made only of spaces is accepted with a success message and saved as a blank-looking rule. An empty pattern is rejected, but spaces aren't trimmed.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, archiving a repository makes its work items read-only. An existing issue in an archived private repository still offers New Issue, but following that button opens Page Not Found instead of an available creation flow or an explanation of the archived restriction.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The issue detail header includes the New Issue link without checking Repository.IsArchived, while the destination rejects archived writes.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, archiving a repository makes its work items read-only. An existing issue in an archived private repository still offers New Issue, but following that button opens Page Not Found instead of an available creation flow or an explanation of the archived restriction.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, issue and pull request (a proposed code change) form actions can expose a raw JSON-parsing SyntaxError labelled Network error when the server rejects an unavailable or unauthorized action. Confirmed triggers include stale deleted/locked/archived comment or issue (a tracked work item) forms, deleted milestone (a named group of work items)/time-entry targets and rejected review actions; the UI does not explain the actual refusal.
logicalBugs.rootCause: fetchActionDoRequest unconditionally calls resp.json() for HTTP 4xx and labels parsing exceptions Network error. Plain-text missing-issue/permission responses therefore expose SyntaxError rather than the rejection reason. Deleted comment inline edits use a separate parser and are kept separate.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, if a repository is archived while a New Issue (or comment) form is open, submitting the form shows a red "Network error SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'N', \"Not found.\" is not valid JSON" instead of saying the repository is archived and read-only.

Open a mergeable pull request, which proposes changes to a repository, and leave its Merge control visible. Archive the repository from another tab, then submit Merge from the stale page. Instead of explaining that an archived repository is read-only, Gitea shows a raw Network error SyntaxError saying Not found. is not valid JSON. The merge is refused.

Open the comparison page’s Create Pull Request form and prepare a proposed change. Archive the repository in another tab, then submit the still-open form. The request is refused, but the page reports a raw Network error SyntaxError about Not found. not being valid JSON rather than explaining the archived, read-only state.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea lets a repository owner grant other accounts access through Collaborators settings. Entering that repository's own owner and choosing Add Collaborator merely reloads the page without explaining why nothing was added, whether the repository belongs to a person or an organization. The owner cannot meaningfully be added again, but the message Cannot add an owner as a collaborator is not shown in this case.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CollaborationPost redirects immediately when the submitted lowercased name equals Repo.Owner.LowerName, without flashing the available owner-collaborator error.
reproductionPaths: On a repository's Collaborators settings, entering the repository's own owner (the user who owns a personal repository, or the organization that owns an organization repository) and clicking Add Collaborator just reloads the page with no error. Gitea already has the message "Cannot add an owner as a collaborator." and shows it when an organization's owner is added, but not for the repository's own owner.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on a public user-owned repository, changing a collaborator from Read to Write or Administrator in Settings > Collaborators shows the new role, even after a reload, but the collaborator's actual permission stays read. The same change on a private repository, or from Write to Administrator, works.
logicalBugs.rootCause: ChangeCollaborationAccessMode updates existing access rows directly with SQL. Public Read collaborators have no explicit access row, so UPDATE affects zero rows rather than inserting/recalculating access.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, on a public user-owned repository, changing a collaborator from Read to Write or Administrator in Settings > Collaborators shows the new role, even after a reload, but the collaborator's actual permission stays read. The same change on a private repository, or from Write to Administrator, works.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a branch protection rule's Protected file patterns field accepts an invalid glob such as '[' and reports success. The pattern is stored as entered, but when it's used the invalid pattern is skipped, so the protected files are no longer protected, with no warning to the repository owner. Tag protection rejects the same invalid pattern when it's saved.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The save path stores ProtectedFilePatterns without compiling them; getFilePatterns logs and skips invalid expressions, leaving no protection for the intended files.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, a branch protection rule's Protected file patterns field accepts an invalid glob such as '[' and reports success. The pattern is stored as entered, but when it's used the invalid pattern is skipped, so the protected files are no longer protected, with no warning to the repository owner. Tag protection rejects the same invalid pattern when it's saved.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, an organization can grant repository access through a team or directly through Settings > Collaborators. A user with a direct Write grant on a public organization repository loses that write access when removed from their last organization team, or otherwise removed from the organization, even though Collaborators still lists Write. Editing the listed role does not restore access. Private repositories and users who remain in another organization team retain the expected direct access.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Removing a member from their last team first recalculates repository access, including direct collaborator grants, then removes the user from the organization. The organization-removal cleanup deletes effective access records for public organization repositories without recreating them from the surviving direct collaborator grants. Subsequent collaborator-role changes only update existing effective access records, so they cannot repair the missing record.
reproductionPaths: Create a public organization repository and give a user Write access both through an organization team and directly as a repository collaborator. Remove that user from their last team in the organization, so their organization membership ends. Collaborators still shows Write, but the user loses write controls such as New Release and file editing; direct creation attempts are refused. Keeping the user in a second organization team or testing a private repository avoids this loss.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a repository with no commits can still have working Wiki, Projects and Packages sections. If Code and Issues are disabled, opening the repository’s home link instead redirects to Pull Requests, which shows 404 because that section requires commits. Disabling Pull Requests can make the same redirect choose Releases and show another 404. This concerns ordinary links to an empty repository’s home selecting an unusable section; a repository with commits can use the same sections normally.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The repository home handler chooses the highest-priority readable enabled section when Code is unavailable, without checking whether that section supports an empty repository. Pull Requests and Releases are guarded by a separate nonempty-repository check, so the selected redirect is rejected even when other readable sections would work.
reproductionPaths: Create a repository without initializing it, leaving it with no commits. Disable Code and Issues in repository settings while leaving Wiki, Projects and Packages enabled. Open the repository from its name in a repository list, header or search result: it redirects to /pulls and shows 404. With Pull Requests disabled as well, it can redirect to /releases and show the same failure; the enabled Wiki, Projects and Packages addresses open normally.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s repository Settings > Collaborators, a user who loses administrator access while the page is open can still click Remove on another collaborator. Confirming closes the dialog with no error, but the collaborator remains because the server refused the removal. The lost permission may result from lowering the user’s own role or another administrator changing it. The defect is the missing failure message; the server correctly prevents the unauthorized deletion.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The collaborator Remove button uses the legacy delete-button handler, which waits for the request but only handles successful HTTP responses. When the administrator permission guard returns an error response, the handler has no error branch, so the confirmation dialog closes without reporting the refusal. This is separate from the role-dropdown handler’s optimistic label update.
reproductionPaths: As a repository administrator who is not its owner, open Settings > Collaborators. Lower your own role to Read without reloading, or have another administrator remove your administrator permission. Click Remove beside a different collaborator and confirm. The dialog closes without an error while the collaborator remains; the same action before losing administrator access removes them and shows a success message.
